recap_lines: Walker is a loop, and git keeps each lap as a commit.
A diff shows what changed, but not that the change works.
A headless run has no window, so a script judges the result.
A hang never ends, so a timeout stops it and counts a failure.
An allow rule pre-approves a command, and a sandbox sets the walls.
A claim says it works, and evidence is a check you can run.
bookends.command: Quiz me on terms for working with a coding agent on a Godot game. Give me short game-making cases, one at a time. Use the terms commit, diff, flag, headless, hang, timeout, allow rule, sandbox, flaky and deterministic. For each case I must name the exact term and say why its look-alike is wrong. Hold back the answer until I reply, then tell me if I was right.
checks: Check: each case is a game-making situation, and the answer waits for you.
Check: you named the exact term and why its look-alike does not fit.

beats.narration_text: This is the Walker loop, six stages in a ring, with a red dot travelling round. Walker is the course's working method and its files, not a program you run. Every change goes round the same loop. Game brief, build, playtest, inspect, revise, export. For example, to add a coin to a platformer, you put the coin in the brief, have the agent build it, play it, inspect what changed, revise, and only then export.
